findings.claim: The plan runs kmctl review due in CI but does not say how the repository is checked out. actions/checkout clones one commit by default (fetch-depth 1), and review-due's third reason (a file in a concept's sources changed in git after its last verified date) reads git history. On a shallow clone every tracked file looks changed in the single fetched commit, or the history lookup fails, so the job summary would report concepts as due when they are not, or skip the reason without saying so. The report would then mean something other than what review-due means locally. The plan needs to state the history requirement (fetch-depth: 0, or the action deepening the clone itself) and what the action does when history is missing. A spike can settle the behaviour: in a temporary repo with two commits, clone with --depth 1 and see what `git log -1 --format=%cI -- PATH` returns for a file last changed in the first commit.

The only done condition is 'the workflow runs green on a pull request here', and the eval has no rows. Meeting it means pushing a branch to github.com/JasperHG90/Knowledge-management and opening a pull request, which the loop's build and review cannot do or check from a local worktree without the operator. 'Green' also depends on this repository's own .okf/ (and its missing docs/) passing kmctl check, which is state this ticket does not own and knowledge-check has not yet defined (for example, whether a missing docs/ folder fails). The plan should either list the remote run as a risk the operator accepts and say who opens the PR, or add a check the loop can run locally (for example, running the action's steps against this repo, and a failing fixture to show the job fails only on kmctl check).
